questions.q: Which compound among the following has the highest dipole moment?
questions.solution:
The dipole moment depends on the charge and distance between the central atom and side atoms. But the charge is more prominent than distance. It is determined as polar and non-polar molecules

It is used for covalent or ionic molecule

μnet = 0 It is for non-polar molecule

μnet ≠0 It is for polar molecule

It can be determined by the geometry of the molecule. As, ammonia has trigonal pyramidal shape in which the dipole moment of lone pair balances the moment of bond pair.

In case of SO2, it have bent shape or V-shape has have net dipole moment towards oxygen atom side.

N2O or CO2 both have the linear shape and so their moment is balanced and so net dipole moment is zero.

Hence, we can conclude that SO2 molecule has a maximum dipole moment.

questions.q: Assuming that the incident radiation is capable of ejecting photo electrons from all the given metals, the lowest kinetic energy of the ejected photoelectron is observed with which of the given metals?
questions.solution:
According to the Einstein's theory of photoelectric effect, for the photoelectric effect to occur, the energy of incident radiation should be greater or equal to the threshold energy called work function of the metal. The equation can be illustrated as:

hν = φ + KEhν - φ =  KE

Now, from above relation it can be said that more will be the work function (φ) of the metal, lesser will be the kinetic energy of the ejected photoelectrons. The order work function for given metals is

Cu>Ag>Li>Na

Therefore, the order of the kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons will be:

Cu<Ag<Li<Na

Hence, Cu possess least K.E. from the given option.

questions.solution: <style type="text/css"><!--td {border: 1px solid #ccc;}br {mso-data-placement:same-cell;}--></style>Thermal expansion is the tendency of matter to change its shape, area, volume, and density in response to a change in temperature, usually not including phase transitions. Thermal expansion generally decreases with increasing bond energy, which also has an effect on the melting point of solids, so, high melting point materials are more likely to have lower thermal expansion. In general, liquids expand slightly more than solids.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a reversible process?
questions.solution: A temperature gradient is a physical quantity that describes in which direction and at what rate the temperature changes in a specific location. Temperature always flows from the hottest to coldest source, due to the fact that cold is nothing but the absence of heat energy.

questions.solution:
In an ideal gas the inter-molecular collisions are assumed to be absent and the collisions are perfectly elastic. Thus, the gas possesses only translational kinetic energy and hence the internal energy of the ideal gas depends only on temperature.

Internal energy, U=32KT

questions.q: What is the shape of the graph between speed and kinetic energy of a body?
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of an object is the energy that it possesses due to its motion. It is defined as the work needed to accelerate a body of a given mass from rest to its stated velocity. Having gained this energy during its acceleration, the body maintains this kinetic energy unless its speed changes.

Kinetic energy, K.E=12mv2∝v2
